summary.text: 明 means “bright” or “clear.” Early accounts preserve two constructions: 日 with 月, associated with brightness or dawn, and 朙, with 月 and a window, interpreted as moonlight entering a room.

formation.text: The evidence supports two early graphic analyses. In the 日+月 form, sun and moon together are associated with brightness or dawn. In 朙, 月 and 囧 (a lattice window) depict moonlight entering a room. 囧 is also proposed as a sound element in 朙, but that role remains disputed: the window’s ancient spoken name is not known, and the available comparisons do not establish a match.

components.text: In the early 日+月 analysis of 明, 日 depicts the sun as part of an image associated with brightness or dawn.
In the early 日+月 analysis of 明, 月 depicts the moon as part of an image associated with brightness or dawn.

In 朙, 囧 is described as a lattice window and contributes the window image. It is also proposed as a sound element, but the role is disputed: the reported Old Chinese forms differ, and the window’s ancient spoken name is not known.

sound_limitation.text: The reported sound role remains unresolved. Baxter–Sagart reconstructions differ, while the similar current Mandarin readings do not establish an ancient correspondence or recover the window’s spoken name.

sound.text: In current Mandarin, 囧 is jiǒng and 明 is míng. Their resemblance does not establish an ancient sound relationship.
In Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese, 囧 is reconstructed as *k-mraŋʔ and 明 as *mraŋ. The forms differ in initial and final, so this comparison alone does not demonstrate the proposed sound role.

components.text: In 朙, 月 depicts the moon in the interpretation of moonlight entering through a window.

history.text: Sun-and-moon forms are reported in oracle-bone and bronze writing. Other early forms include 朙, analyzed as 月 and 囧, as well as less secure 目+月 and 田+月 forms. Shuowen identifies 明 as an ancient form of 朙; this does not make 朙 the sole early construction.
A Qin manuscript’s 目-form is reported as a likely graphic corruption of 囧. This concerns the written form and does not resolve how the distinct early constructions relate.

uncertainties.text: The reported early forms and readings come from dictionary accounts; the underlying inscription images were not inspected, and exact dates for the cited examples remain unresolved.

senses.text: Brightness is reported among the uses of oracle-bone examples. The evidence does not show whether this use preceded or followed the attested dawn use.
Dawn is reported among the uses of oracle-bone examples; a Shijing line also illustrates daybreak. Its chronological relation to the brightness sense is unresolved.
Clear or manifest uses are reported in bronze inscriptions. How this sense developed from brightness or dawn is not shown.
Current meanings include bright, light, and clear.

limitations.text: The relative chronology of the early brightness and dawn uses, and the development of later clear or manifest uses, remain unresolved.

overview.text: 明 means “bright” or “clear.” Early accounts show a sun-and-moon form associated with brightness or dawn, and another form, 朙, with moon and window suggesting moonlight. The window’s proposed sound role is uncertain.

components.text: 日 pictures the sun in the early sun-and-moon analysis.
月 pictures the moon in the early sun-and-moon analysis.
In 朙, 囧 pictures a lattice window; its proposed sound role is uncertain.
In 朙, 月 pictures the moon in the moonlight-through-a-window interpretation.

relationships.text: In the early 日+月 analysis, 日 depicts the sun as part of the celestial image associated with 明.
In the early 日+月 analysis, 月 depicts the moon as part of the celestial image associated with 明.
Shuowen identifies 明 as an ancient form of 朙, whose analysis joins 月 and 囧. This does not show that 朙 was the only early construction.
In 朙, 囧 is described as a lattice window and contributes the window image.
In 朙, 月 depicts the moon in the moonlight-through-a-window interpretation.

囧 is proposed as a sound element in 朙. Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstructions for 囧 (*k-mraŋʔ) and 明 (*mraŋ) differ in initial and final; current Mandarin jiǒng and míng resemble one another but do not settle the historical analysis. The window’s ancient spoken name is not established.
